messages:
Liam (AE): Heads-up 10: Big banking RFP: Private deploy required. Requirements: preserve L4 client IPs (no SNAT), static egress IPs for allowlisting, and contractual burst headroom (2x baseline for 15m). Any immediate blockers?
Asha (SE): Quick clarifier: do they require cross-account TGW attachments or are VPC peering + shared routes acceptable? Also: are they OK with us pushing logs to their SIEM or do they want Redwood-managed retention?
Dana (Customer): Cross-account TGW is OK with approvals. SIEM ingestion preferred (customer-managed Kinesis/Logstash). No managed NAT allowed.
Tom (NetOps): For raw 5-tuple preservation we must avoid any SNAT in the data path. Options: 1) TGW attachment with route tables pointing to our connector subnets (recommended) 2) VPC peering with explicit routes 3) Azure: ExpressRoute/private peering into our partner VNet. PrivateLink is only an option if app-layer headers (X-Forwarded-For) are acceptable.
Yuri (Solutions Eng): Security checklist to give them:
```
- Route table: point specific prefix (we provide) to tgw-attachment or peering
- SGs: allow inbound from connector CIDRs on TCP/443, health TCP/80
- DNS: allow outbound to their resolvers; fallback to 1.1.1.1 if allowed
- MTU: test 1500; account for IPsec overhead
- Logs: configure Kinesis/S3 endpoint for log delivery (we'll provide IAM policy)
```
Asha (SE): Egress IPs: best practice is reserved EIP pool attached to dedicated egress instances. BYOIP possible but longer lead time. Note: on-demand EIPs can hit account quotas during bursts.
Liam (AE): Pricing/SLA question: can we offer a burst throughput SLA?
Tom (NetOps): Commercially: connector uptime SLA is straightforward. Burst throughput SLA requires Dedicated reserved nodes + contractual throughput SLO and pre-warmed capacity. Otherwise bursts are best-effort. Finance ballpark: baseline 300 rps ~$11k/mo; burst addon ~30% (region dependent).
Dana (Customer): For audit we need a short vendor statement about how client IPs are handled and where logs live. Can you draft?
Yuri (Solutions Eng): Draft para: "Redwood Private supports Transit Gateway attachments, VPC peering, and cloud private peering (ExpressRoute). For transport-layer client IP preservation, customers should use TGW or VPC peering and avoid SNAT in the path. Static egress IPs are available via reserved EIP pools attached to dedicated egress instances; BYOIP arrangements supported in select regions. Logs containing client IPs can be forwarded to customer-managed SIEM (Kinesis/S3) or retained in Redwood-managed encrypted buckets as per contract; KMS keys can be customer-managed."
Asha (SE): Operational caveat: TGW route propagation can take a few minutes; plan a maintenance window for cutover. Also, if we deploy any routed EC2 hosts, we must disable source/dest checks.
Tom (NetOps): Testing runbook snippet to hand to their netops:
```
# verify path & client IP preservation	route -n
traceroute -T -p 443 <connector-eip>
sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host <client-ip> and port 443
# latency check
curl -w "%{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://<connector-eip>/healthz
```
Dana (Customer): Good. Also need assurance logs with client IPs remain in-region and encrypted with our KMS if possible.
Yuri (Solutions Eng): We can support customer-managed KMS for Redwood-managed storage (requires Enterprise contract). We'll call this out in the architecture doc.
NetOpsBot: Preflight ticket created: https://redwood.internal/tickets/CXN-10234 (contains TGW/peering checklist, EIP reservation steps, and test scripts).
Liam (AE): Next steps: Asha to produce 1-page arch diagram (TGW + peering variants) + allowlist by EOD tomorrow; Yuri to send questionnaire paragraph and log/KMS details; schedule tech huddle Fri 10am PT with customer's netsec.
Dana (Customer): Fri 10am PT works. Thanks everyone.
Liam (AE): I'll create the invite and attach the ticket + runbook. :thumbsup:
